subject: Service reliability review & premium commitment path for Arcadia Analytics
messages:
From: Sara Huang <sara@arcadia-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kyle Ramsey <kyle.ramsey@arcadia-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Action] Short-term uptime/latency impact across transactions API

Hi Ben —

We saw a repeated pattern of tail-latency spikes across our transactions API between 08:30–09:10 PST this morning (p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.8s for a sustained ~20 minutes). This has caused a handful of downstream timeouts and two support tickets from enterprise customers. We've attached a small bundle of traces and p95/p99 histograms (arcadia_latency_logs.zip) for your engineering team.

Given the impact, procurement has asked whether Redwood can 1) provide an exception to the current renewal terms to qualify Arcadia for a premium SLA immediately, and 2) commit to a short remediation plan and credit for the incident window. We are in a renewal conversation that will be impacted by how quickly we can stabilize and by the commercial remedy.

Concrete asks:
- Can Redwood make a short-term premium pilot available (dedicated or reserved pool) within two weeks?
- If the pilot is accepted, can we get an elevated SLA (regional p95/p99 targets) and a temporary discount while ramping?
- Can you confirm what diagnostic/mitigation steps you plan to take in the next 48 hours so we can communicate to our ops team?

We can be available for a 30-min call today at 2pm PT.

—Sara
Sara Huang
Head of Platform Operations
Arcadia Analytics

Attachment: arcadia_latency_logs.zip

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Huang <sara@arcadia-analytics.com>
Cc: Kyle Ramsey <kyle.ramsey@arcadia-analytics.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Action] Short-term uptime/latency impact across transactions API

Sara — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. I'm really sorry for the disruption. We take reliability seriously and want to get you a clear remediation and commercial path.

I looped in our SRE and CS leads (Markus, Evelyn) to triage. We can do 2pm PT today — I sent a calendar invite. Top-level next steps from my side:
- Internal triage now (Markus) to validate the traces and confirm root-cause hypothesis.
- If there is capacity/serving config work needed, we can scope whether a short-term dedicated pool pilot (2–6 weeks) is the fastest way to stabilize.
- Commercially, I will work with Evelyn to propose a one-time incident credit and an expedited premium onboarding offer if we can commit to an SLO map you sign off on.

I'll follow up after the triage call with a concrete mitigation plan and timeline.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: invite.ics)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Sara Huang <sara@arcadia-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Action] Short-term uptime/latency impact across transactions API

On Sun, Aug 16, 2026 at 9:14 AM Sara Huang <sara@arcadia-analytics.com> wrote:
> We saw a repeated pattern of tail-latency spikes across our transactions API...

Thanks for the logs — preliminary read: the spikes correlate with occasional long KV-cache miss latencies (rare host-level GC outliers + background checkpointing on the serving nodes). The pattern looks like a small number of requests get pushed to the cold path and hit slower kernels.

What I'll try immediately (next 2–4 hours):
- Adjust prefix/KV cache TTLs for Arcadia's keyspace to reduce cold-path misses.
- Reduce max batching window for the transactions route to lower tail exposure for small requests.
- Pin a pilot nodegroup with slightly higher CPU affinity to reduce background jitter.

If you can provide the per-shard telemetry and any recent model change timestamps (we saw a minor config roll last week), send those and I'll correlate. Longer term, a short Dedicated pool avoids noisy-neighbor surface from multi-tenant batching and will likely reduce the tail significantly; estimate 48–72h to stand up a pilot and 3–5 days to validate under production traffic.

I'll post a brief runbook after the call.

—Markus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
(Attachment requested: per-shard-telemetry.csv)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial proposal framing for Arcadia — credit & pilot

Team — summary of the commercial levers we can offer quickly for renewal conversations:

1) Incident credit: offer 10% one-time credit against last invoice for the affected window (standard for this severity).
2) Dedicated pilot: 6-week pilot with a 20% onboarding discount (covers set-up + reserved capacity). If the pilot is successful and Arcadia converts to a Dedicated plan, we amortize the pilot fee into the first quarter of committed spend.
3) SLA elevation: Commit to an SLO map for the pilot window (regional p95 < 200ms, regional p99 < 800ms) with a rollback/fallback clause to the baseline if not met after validation.
4) Procurement acceleration: provide a pre-filled SLA exception form (SLA_exception_form.pdf) and expedited DOCS/PO process — procurement will need a DocuSign link and a short Term Sheet.

Risks/notes: we should avoid promising credits beyond standard incident policy without exec approval. If Arcadia asks for an immediate long-term SLA upgrade we need legal sign-off.

I'll draft a short commercial note for Ben to send to the customer that includes timelines and the HubSpot deal link (https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/DEAL-8472).

—Evelyn
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Huang <sara@arcadia-analytics.com>, Kyle Ramsey <kyle.ramsey@arcadia-analytics.com>, procurement@arcadia-analytics.com
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: short-term Dedicated pilot + incident credit (Arcadia Analytics)

Sara/Kyle — thanks again for the call and for sharing the logs. Based on the triage and internal review, here is the proposed path to stabilize operations and de-risk the renewal: 

Proposal (action items):
1) Short-term Dedicated pilot
   - 6-week pilot (start target: within 10 business days from signed agreement).
   - Reserved nodegroup sized to match your current 95th percentile throughput.
   - Pilot onboarding fee (waived at 20% discount for pilot convert-to-commit scenario).

2) Incident credit
   - One-time account credit equal to 10% of the last invoice, applied upon pilot start.

3) Measurable SLOs during pilot
   - Regional p95 target: <200ms; regional p99 target: <800ms.
   - Weekly quality checks and an SLO validation report at weeks 2, 4, and 6.

4) Next steps for procurement
   - I've attached the SLA exception form (SLA_exception_form.pdf) and a pre-filled Term Sheet. Please return a signed DocuSign (link below) so we can provision the pilot.

Links and attachments:
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/DEAL-8472
- Incident logs (read-only): https://drive.google.com/arcadia/incident-logs
- SLA exception: SLA_exception_form.pdf

If this path looks reasonable, we'll get legal and finance to prepare an expedited DocuSign and provisioning checklist. If you'd rather try an operational configuration first, Markus can continue with the TTL and batching changes immediately and we can re-evaluate after 48–72h.

Proposed timeline: sign by Aug 28 -> pilot provisioned by Sep 2 -> validation through mid-September.

Appreciate the urgency — Ben will coordinate procurement and Evelyn will own onboarding.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
